VARMA\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); clear: both; color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; text-align: center;\"\u003ERoll no: 67\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\" \/\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EThis blog is my learning experience in medicine posting, which was from 12 December 2022 to 11 February 2022.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EICU ROTATION\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EMy first clinical rotation was in the peripheral postings, of which I started off my medicine posting in the Intensive care unit (ICU) for the first 5 days.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"color: #757575;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); font-size: 15px;\"\u003EEven though the ICU duty only last for a short amount of time, it is an opportunity to learn a lot of clinical skills. Starting with ICU made me dive head first into the critical care aspect of medicine, and it was a challenge to acclimatise so quickly to a fast paced environment.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"color: #757575;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); font-size: 15px;\"\u003EHowever, even though it was initially a struggle, the PGs made it an easy transition, and I was able to learn a lot in my time there.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"color: #757575;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); font-size: 15px;\"\u003EWhen I was posted in the ICU, it was a full house, with 7 ICU patient and 9 AMC patients to monitor. I got the opportunity to learn how to draw ABG samples, taking around 15 radial and femoral samples as well as drawing regular blood samples for to send as lab samples.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"color: #757575;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); font-size: 15px;\"\u003EI learned how to place a nasogastric (ryles) tube, and was able to place it for 4 patients. I also learned how to insert a foleys catheter for both female and male patients in the ICU.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"color: #757575;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); font-size: 15px;\"\u003EI was able to assist the PGs with the placement of a central line for a nephrology patient that got shifted to the ICU.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EI was able to Assist during active management of a patient who went into cardiac arrest.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EHe was a 65 year old male with CKD on MHD. The patient was shifted to AMC from nephro ward as his blood pressure was around 70\/40 mmhg . Norad was connected and dose was being increased as his blood pressure was falling. I checked his BP and it was not recordable and the pulse was feeble. And immediately the patient was shifted to ICU and was intubated. After 20 minutes pulse was not recordable and CPR was done for 30 minutes.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EI monitored patients during blood transfusion and learned about transfusion reactions.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EI was able to learn properly about blood pressure lower medications in patient with CKD as I had a 25 year old male patient on dialysis for nephrology who was in the AMC. He had continuous BP recording of around 200\/100 and I was able to learn the dose and choice medications for these patients.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr class=\"Apple-interchange-newline\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; caret-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); color: black;\" \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003ENEPHROLOGY ROTATION\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EAfter ICU, I was placed into nephrology duties for the next five days. Nephrology was by far my most challenging posting, just for the sheer amount of work as well as the condition of the patients.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EIn nephrology, we are expected to take care of all the ICU\/AMC nephrology cases and CKD ward patients who are our inpatients, as well as the patients who come daily for maintenance hemodialysis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EDuring my nephrology rotation, I monitored 2 PRBC blood transfusions and was able to learn about the use of cross matching samples, figured out donors, and learned about transfusion reactions.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EI also assisted Dr Pavani maam in the placement of two central lines.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EOne of the best opportunities was to sit in for the dialysis sessions and be able to learn how the equipment works and how patients react to hemo dialysis. I monitored around 10 patients in different sessions of hemo dialysis and was able to do vital monitoring, learn about different complications that could arise, the benefits or disadvantages of placing a patient on hemo dialysis etc.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EIt was a great learning experience, and even though nephrology was an intense posting, I really enjoyed it.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EWARD ROTATIONS\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EMy last 5 days of peripheral postings consisted of ward duties. Ward postings were one of my favourite postings, because you get to see patients from all units of general medicine.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EDuring my time there, I was able to see different cases in the ICU\/AMC\/Ward that were taken care of my other units and was able to take my own history for some patients.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EOne such example is a case of a 35 year old female who came to casualty with fever and thrombocytopenia who was on ART for the past 10 years.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EThis is the blog link of the case that I made, and I actually followed this patient from the time of admission into casualty, because I was working a replacement shift in casualty when she got admitted.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/blog\/post\/edit\/7266053451185593900\/8734423051916860159\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.blogger.com\/blog\/post\/edit\/7266053451185593900\/8734423051916860159\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EThis case also helped me understand the value of doctor patient communication. Due to the casualty being extremely busy that night, the patient had initially only been put on basic medications and was yet to be evaluated around 2 hours after coming to casualty. Naturally, her attender was anxious and threatened to leave the hospital and complain about lack of care. My PG was kind enough to let me talk to the patient and attender and I was able to explain the situation and about how we had done the initial work up and there was nothing to worry about. It was a valuable lesson in an area that is taken for granted, and the value of communication to the patient should never be taken lightly, it can do wonders in reassuring the patient.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EOnce this case got discharged, we created a PAJR group for follow up complaints and treatment efficacy, as well as to monitor her ART regimen and CD4 counts.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EThere were other interesting cases like this that I had the opportunity to look at, and the ward duties turned out to be one of my favourite learning experiences because of the amount of patient interaction that I was able to do.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EUNIT DUTY\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EMy next 4 weeks included being posted into the main general medicine units. I was placed into first unit under Dr Zain Alam, Dr Raveen, Dr Prachetan and Dr Vivek.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EUnit duties mainly consist of OP days, along with looking after casualty cases and overall monitoring and treatment regimens of the patients that get admitted under your care.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EThese are the blog links of some interesting cases that I saw admitted during my time in unit-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EUnit duty was a great opportunity to be able to learn how to handle a multitude of patients and about treatment and evaluation of different cases.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EOur OP days are on Monday’s, and we see around 80-100 cases per day. We were able to learn how to take patient history and do clinical examinations for many patients.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EWith the help of our PGs we had the opportunity to look at different clinical cases and do real time application of evaluation and coming to a conclusion about the diagnosis and treatment regimens of the patients.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPSYCHIATRY POSTINGS\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EMy last 15 days of medicine was in the department of psychiatry.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EPsychiatry is a subject that I’m very interested in, and it was a great opportunity to be able to look at different cases and watch the PGs evaluate each case, because it’s a different approach than what we’re used to in medicine.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003ESome cases we saw included schizophrenia, panic attacks, depression etc.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; Since then, the patient is on regular diabetic medication.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- H\/O of burning sensation and tingling in both lower limbs since 1 year\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- Patient is having slurring of speech and deviation of mouth to the right side since yesterday morning\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- No H\/O weakness of limbs, seizures, trauma, headache\/nausea, or fever.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- K\/C\/O DM type 2 since the last 10 years (on regular medication, Glimi M1)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEXAMINATION\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPt is C\/C\/C\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBP:130\/80mm hg\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPR:96bpm\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERR:20\/min\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGRBS- 261\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETemp : Afebrile\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;
